An image display system includes a display device, storage means, and display control means. The system is configured to receive an input operation performed on a first display object displayed on the display device, and to acquire operation information relating to that input operation. The operation information includes at least a moving direction and a moving amount of an input position during the input operation.

When the acquired operation information indicates that the input position has moved in a predetermined first direction by an amount exceeding a predetermined threshold, the system acquires a first attribute parameter of the first display object. The first attribute parameter corresponds to the predetermined first direction in which the input position has moved.

The storage means stores a plurality of display objects. Each display object is associated with one or more attribute parameters. When the movement in the predetermined first direction exceeds the threshold, the system searches the storage means for a second display object associated with the first display object. The second display object is extracted when it has a first attribute parameter that is different from the first attribute parameter of the first display object.

After the second display object has been extracted, the display control means controls the display device to display the second display object in place of the first display object. In this manner, the image display system changes the displayed object according to the direction and amount of movement of the input position during the input operation, using attribute parameters associated with the display objects to determine an appropriate replacement object.
outputs.L4:
An image display system is configured to display an object, such as an image, icon, document, content item, or other visual element, and to receive an input operation performed with respect to that displayed object. The input operation may be made, for example, by a user dragging a finger on a touch panel, moving a cursor with a pointing device, operating a controller, or performing another gesture-like movement. When the operation is detected, the system determines both the direction of movement and the amount of movement. The direction may correspond to one of a plurality of predefined directions, such as upward, downward, leftward, or rightward movement, and the amount of movement may be measured as a distance, displacement, speed, or accumulated operation value.

Each movement direction is associated with a particular attribute parameter of the displayed object. For example, a horizontal movement may correspond to a first attribute, while a vertical movement may correspond to a second attribute. The attribute parameter may represent any property or classification that links the currently displayed object to other related objects, such as time, category, location, sequence, type, priority, version, color, size, file group, or another metadata value. By associating different directions with different attribute parameters, the system allows a user to select the type of relationship to be used for switching or navigating among display objects simply by choosing the direction of the input movement.

The system compares the detected movement amount with a predetermined threshold value. If the movement amount does not exceed the threshold, the system may maintain the current display state, provide a temporary visual response, or wait for further input. If the movement amount exceeds the threshold, the system determines that a valid swipe-like operation has been performed. In response, the system selects the attribute parameter associated with the detected movement direction and identifies another display object that is related to the currently displayed object through that selected attribute parameter.

Once the related object has been identified, the system replaces the currently displayed object with the related object. The replacement object has a corresponding attribute value that differs from that of the previously displayed object, while still being associated with it according to the selected attribute parameter. For instance, if the selected direction corresponds to chronological order, the system may display an image taken before or after the current image. If the selected direction corresponds to category, the system may display another item in a different category or in a related classification. If the direction corresponds to location, the system may switch to another image or object associated with a different place.

This operation enables intuitive navigation among related display items without requiring the user to open menus, select filters, or manually search through a list. A simple directional movement is sufficient to specify both the intended navigation command and the attribute relationship to be used. Because the system only performs the replacement when the movement amount exceeds a threshold, accidental or minor movements can be ignored, improving reliability and ease of use. The result is an image display interface that allows users to switch among associated objects in a natural, swipe-based manner while preserving meaningful relationships between the displayed items.

An image display is a visual presentation of pictures, graphics, or digital content on a screen or other medium. It allows users to view photographs, illustrations, designs, advertisements, and information in a clear and engaging way. Image displays are used in many places, including websites, smartphones, digital cameras, museums, stores, and public information boards.

A good image display should be bright, sharp, and easy to understand. High resolution helps show small details, while proper color balance makes the image look natural and attractive. The size and layout of the display also matter, especially when several images are shown together. For example, an online gallery may use a grid layout so visitors can browse many pictures quickly.

Image displays are important in communication because visuals often capture attention faster than words. They can tell a story, explain an idea, or promote a product. In business, an effective image display can make a brand look more professional and appealing. In education, images can help students understand complex topics more easily.

Today, image display technology continues to improve. Modern screens offer better brightness, deeper contrast, and more realistic colors. Whether used for entertainment, learning, advertising, or art, an image display is a powerful tool for sharing visual information.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent abstract describing a display device that detects movement direction and amount of an input operation on a first display object, extracts an associated second display object based on attribute parameters when a threshold is exceeded, and displays it instead.
counterfactuals.output: A display device includes a display unit, an input detection unit, and a controller. When the movement amount exceeds the threshold value, the controller extracts, from among a plurality of display objects, a second display object associated with the first display object based on attribute parameters corresponding to the detected movement direction. counterfactuals.output:
In some embodiments, a computer-implemented method is provided for interactive image substitution. The method comprises displaying, by a computing device, a first image in a graphical user interface; detecting, by the computing device, a user input comprising a drag or swipe gesture applied to the first image; determining that the drag or swipe gesture is in a predetermined direction and exceeds a threshold distance, velocity, duration, or combination thereof; identifying, based at least in part on the predetermined direction, an image attribute associated with the first image; selecting, from a plurality of associated images, a second image having a value of the identified image attribute that differs from a corresponding value of the identified image attribute of the first image; and replacing display of the first image with display of the second image in the graphical user interface.

In some embodiments, the identified image attribute comprises one or more of a color, style, pose, orientation, expression, configuration, product feature, time, location, category, or other visual or metadata-based characteristic. In some embodiments, different gesture directions are mapped to different attributes, such that a swipe in a first direction corresponds to a first attribute and a swipe in a second direction corresponds to a second attribute. In some embodiments, the plurality of associated images are linked to the first image by metadata, an image database, a product catalog, a content graph, or a machine-learning-based similarity or association model.

In some embodiments, selecting the second image comprises identifying an image associated with the first image that differs primarily with respect to the identified attribute while maintaining one or more other attributes substantially unchanged. In some embodiments, replacing the first image comprises animating a transition from the first image to the second image in a direction corresponding to the detected drag or swipe gesture.

In some embodiments, a non-transitory computer-readable medium stores instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising displaying a first image, detecting a directional drag or swipe input applied to the first image, determining that the directional drag or swipe input satisfies a threshold condition, identifying an attribute corresponding to a direction of the input, retrieving or selecting a second image associated with the first image and having a different value for the identified attribute, and causing the second image to be displayed in place of the first image.

In some embodiments, a system comprises one or more processors and memory storing instructions executable by the one or more processors to display a current image, receive a gesture input relative to the current image, determine a direction and magnitude of the gesture input, compare the magnitude to a threshold, identify an attribute mapped to the determined direction when the magnitude exceeds the threshold, determine an associated replacement image having a value of the identified attribute different from a value of the current image, and update a display to replace the current image with the associated replacement image.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
